stage1.impression: A clean architectural visualisation seen through a shopfront: oak shelves of tinted globe lamps, a terrazzo plinth, and a slatted oak box at the back under a pale glowing band. It is lit like a bright evening showroom, not a night bar: everything is evenly visible, the LED shelf lines are blown, the terrazzo is coarse and over-bright, the plaster and oak are smooth CG, and the many candy-coloured globes pull the eye away from the lantern. A design magazine would read it as a generic, well-modelled bar render, not a specific place it photographed.

blocking_9: Frame reads as night: whole-frame lum_median 22-50 (now 105.6), with the lantern band the brightest thing in the room and pools of light separated by real dark
The lantern band reads amber, not pale pink/white: band region delta_e to #E0902A < 12 (now 29.4) and clip_pct < 1 (now 5.3)
The lantern is the hero at a glance: band and baffle are clearly brighter than the shop's shelves, plinth and side wall (now the plinth, at 201.6, outshines the baffle, at 133)
Materials hold up at 1:1: terrazzo with fine chips and a darker honed ground, lime plaster with trowel variation, oak with real grain and end variation, no evenly smooth CG walls

Some sign of life and atmosphere: glasses or a bottle on the counter and table, a record out of its sleeve, faint visible haze in the light beams, and a believable faint street reflection on the glass
No blown LED lines: shelf and back-bar strips bright but not clipping white

defects.what: Overall overexposed for a night interior; lum_median 105.6, only 28.8% of pixels below 40
Acrylic fin band reads pale pink-white and flat, 5.3% clipped, no fin structure or amber colour (delta_e 29.4 to amber)
Shelf LED strip lines are blown thin white lines that read as signage or display-case lighting
Window plinth terrazzo is the brightest large surface (median 201.6), with oversized chips that read as gravel or granite at this scale
Terrazzo floor is a uniform speckle with no honed sheen, pool or reflection from the lights
Lime plaster wall is a flat, evenly lit smooth grey (median 112) with a CG gradient, no trowel texture and no pool or falloff from a fixture
A row of saturated tinted globes (red, green, cyan, violet, etc.) on the shelves competes with the lantern for colour and attention, reading as a shop display
Globe lamps on the plinth sit like props on a showroom plinth, evenly spaced, with no shadow-casting light of their own
Lantern baffle slats and box are evenly lit pinkish oak (median 133) with a soft, featureless top-to-bottom fall-off, not a grazing light that shows the slots
The foreground mullion is a soft, uniform bar (edge width 37 px) with no glass reflection or street light on it; the glass itself shows no reflection
The ceiling is a near-empty dark void with a glossy streak, and no fixtures or structure read
The counter and bar have no glasses, bottles or records: no sign of life anywhere in the frame
Pendants read as tinted plastic (a violet and a salmon shade) and add colours that are neither neutral nor the hero

changes.problem: The frame is exposed like a dusk showroom, not a night room; the median is more than twice the ceiling of the target range.
changes.expected: The whole frame drops by roughly 1.5 stops: lum_median about 40, deep shadows between the pools, and practicals still bright

changes.problem: The lantern's acrylic band is clipped to a pale pink-white strip, so it reads as a lightbox sign, not amber fins.

change.setting: the lantern's band: emission (and its colour temperature)
change.to: 1.6 at 2200 K, so the Smoke fins tint it amber and each fin's polished edge carries a brighter line

changes.expected: The band glows saturated amber with visible fin rhythm and edges, unclipped, and remains the brightest surface in the room

changes.problem: The window plinth is the brightest large surface in the frame and steals the eye from the lantern.

change.setting: the route area light and the fill; the terrazzo ground tone
change.from: route 0.3 W/m2, fill 0.06 W/m2, light ground
change.to: route 0.08 W/m2, fill 0.02 W/m2; terrazzo ground darkened by about 30% (a warm mid-grey)

changes.expected: The plinth sits in shadow, lit only by the globes' own small pools; it is clearly darker than the lantern baffle

changes.problem: The shelf and back-bar LED lines are blown thin white strokes that read as display-case signage.

evidence.measured: p95 203, thin lines at the white point, clip_pct 0.11 in the shelf column

change.to: 1.5, set back behind a lip so only the wash on the oak shows, not the strip

changes.expected: The shelves get a warm wash with no visible white lines; the column reads as furniture and falls back behind the lantern

changes.problem: The lime plaster wall is evenly lit like a daylit render wall, with no pool and no texture.

change.from: fill 0.06 W/m2; banquette 4 x 9 W at 24 deg
change.to: fill 0.02 W/m2; banquette 4 x 9 W at 18 deg aimed to graze the plaster from 0.3 m off the wall, and plaster bump strength raised so the trowel texture reads

changes.expected: The plaster is mostly dark with scalloped grazed pools showing trowel texture above the banquette

changes.problem: The lantern's slotted baffle is lit flatly, so the slots and depth do not read and it does not look like a lit object.

evidence.measured: lum_median 133, falloff bins 147 to 87 top to bottom, soft and even

change.to: 1 x area 1.2 W/m2, 2400 K, as a narrow strip tight to the baffle top so the light grazes down the slats

changes.expected: After the exposure drop, the baffle stays the second-brightest surface, with a strong top-to-bottom gradient and dark slots between lit slats

changes.problem: Nothing in the frame says anyone is here; it reads as an empty showroom.

evidence.measured: the counter and table tops are empty apart from the lamps

change.to: two half-full rocks glasses and a bottle on the counter, a record out of its sleeve and a glass on the shop table, a coat on a banquette end

changes.expected: Small highlights on glass at the counter and table, and a sign of life

changes.problem: The terrazzo chips are oversized and high-contrast, and the floor lacks a honed sheen, so at 1:1 it reads as gravel or a CG granite texture.

evidence.measured: large chips visible at 2x crop; floor 230-1180 x 540-690 is a uniform speckle, lum_range 154

change.setting: terrazzo chip size and ground tone (finish within kind); haze
change.from: coarse chips, light ground, matte; haze 0.003
change.to: chips about 40% of the current size with lower contrast, a darker warm ground, roughness 0.25 so the lights leave soft pools and reflections; haze 0.006 per metre

changes.expected: The floor and plinth read as honed terrazzo at scale, with soft reflected pools under the lights and faint visible air in the beams

out_of_scope.request: Reduce the number of saturated tinted Core lamps on the shelves and plinth, or the coloured pendant shades, so the frame has one colour
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes EARF's products as placed (the Cores and Hemispheres in tints). They cost the 'one colour' criterion and are the main reason the frame reads as a shop display rather than a specific bar. The owner should decide whether this shot carries fewer tints or a crop that excludes most of them.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Tropos pair or Mother EARF visible as the hero speaker
out_of_scope.why: From the street, no speaker reads; the hero is the lantern. Changing what is visible needs a camera or architecture decision. A camera move is allowed but would change the frame's purpose (the passer-by view).
